instructions: Cuts YouTube videos to a time range and returns full transcripts as a file, plus a short TLDR of the best take. For anyone who wants clips and captions back without doing the download themselves.

skills.name: Clip YouTube
skills.description: Use this when the user wants a clip, cut, or transcript from a YouTube URL (or a local video) for a time range.
skills.content:
---
name: Clip YouTube
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants a clip, cut, or transcript from a YouTube URL (or
  a local video) for a time range.
---
Turn a YouTube URL (or a local video file) plus a time range into a playable MP4 clip, and optionally a sliced transcript.

Need from the user: a URL or local file path, and start and end timestamps (e.g. 6:17–7:21). If either is missing, ask once. Default the range to the last clip in the conversation when they say "same range" or "another one."

Do not overwrite earlier clips. Name outputs from a short sanitized title plus the range, e.g. Title-6m17-7m21.mp4.

Tools: ensure yt-dlp and ffmpeg/ffprobe are on PATH before downloading. Prefer existing binaries. On Linux, install ffmpeg via apt and current yt-dlp via pipx (not the distro yt-dlp). On macOS, brew install yt-dlp ffmpeg. If yt-dlp lives in ~/.local/bin, export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH". Never scrape browser cookies.

Cut a clip:
1. Print title and duration (no download) and confirm the video is long enough for the range.
2. Download only that section with yt-dlp using --download-sections "*START-END" and --force-keyframes-at-cuts, merge to mp4. Use clock times in the section (*6:17-7:21), not a guessed second count. 6:17 is 377s, not 397s.
3. Make the file widely playable: H.264 + AAC stereo MP4 with faststart. If the source is AV1, re-encode to H.264. Remux with ffmpeg -c copy -movflags +faststart when already H.264.
4. Verify with ffprobe: duration matches the range (about 1s slop is fine), video and audio present.
If YouTube 403s or bot-checks, retry with --extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android". If there is a JS runtime warning and formats are missing, keep going if the download succeeded.

Transcript when asked: subs only, no video. yt-dlp --skip-download --write-subs --write-auto-subs --sub-langs "en.*,it.*,en,it" --convert-subs srt. Add other langs the user named. Prefer manual English over auto. Convert VTT to SRT with ffmpeg if --convert-subs did not run. Slice cues that overlap the window. Auto-captions roll and duplicate: for a readable .txt, keep the last line of each cue and drop consecutive dupes. Light-fix obvious ASR glitches only. Say whether subs were manual or auto. Deliver the cleaned transcript in chat and the .srt as a file. Extra langs: same slice, only if those tracks actually existed.

Deliver the MP4 (and srt/transcript if requested). Mention duration, resolution, and if captions were auto-only.

skills.name: Transcripts
skills.description: Use this when the user wants the full transcript of a YouTube (or local) video as a file, plus a short TLDR of the best take.
skills.content:
---
name: Transcripts
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants the full transcript of a YouTube (or local) video
  as a file, plus a short TLDR of the best take.
---
Pull the full transcript of a video with yt-dlp, send it back as a file, and add a short TLDR of the best take.

This is the whole-video job. For a timed clip plus sliced captions, use Clip YouTube instead.

Need from the user: a YouTube URL or a local video/audio path. If they also name languages, use those. Default to English, and include Italian when they usually want it or the video is in Italian. If they name a time range, still get the full transcript, then also slice that window in the file.

Tools: ensure yt-dlp and ffmpeg are on PATH (export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" when yt-dlp is pipx-installed). Install current yt-dlp via pipx, not the distro package. Never scrape browser cookies. On 403 / bot-check, retry with --extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android".

Get captions with yt-dlp --skip-download --write-subs --write-auto-subs --sub-langs "en.*,it.*,en,it" --convert-subs srt. Prefer manual subs over auto. If --convert-subs does not run, convert VTT to SRT with ffmpeg. Note whether captions were official or auto-generated. If there are no captions at all, say so. Do not invent a transcript. Whisper/local ASR is only if the user asks to transcribe from audio.

Clean into a readable file. Auto-captions roll and duplicate. Build a .txt: keep the last line of each cue, drop consecutive duplicate lines, light-fix obvious ASR glitches only, keep timestamps as [m:ss] or [h:mm:ss] at paragraph breaks, not on every fragment. Write WORKDIR/<short-title>.transcript.txt (readable, this is the file to send) and WORKDIR/<short-title>.en.srt. Same for Italian or other requested langs when those tracks exist, as a separate file. Do not dump the raw overlapping auto-caption SRT into chat.

TLDR of the best take: read the cleaned transcript and write 3–6 sentences. What the video is (speakers, topic) in one line. The best take: the sharpest claim, story, or quote worth clipping, with an approximate timestamp so it can be cut later. One extra beat only if it is actually strong. Do not recap the whole episode. Do not hedge with "the video discusses many topics." Pick a take.

Deliver: send the TLDR in chat (best take + timestamp first). Attach the .transcript.txt file (and other lang/srt files if they exist and were requested). Mention auto vs official captions in a short aside, not a report.
